statement:"∀ f : KdVPlan.Coeff, (∀ (N : ℝ) (j : ℤ), ‖KdVPlan.cutoff N f j‖ ≤ ‖f j‖) ∧ (∀ (j : ℤ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, KdVPlan.cutoff (n : ℝ) f j = f j) ∧ (KdVPlan.ZeroMean f → ∀ N : ℝ, KdVPlan.ZeroMean (KdVPlan.cutoff N f))",
proof:"intro f
refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
· intro N j
  unfold KdVPlan.cutoff
  split_ifs <;> simp
· intro j
  filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_ge_atTop j.natAbs] with n hn
  apply if_pos
  have hr : |(j : ℝ)| = (j.natAbs : ℝ) := by norm_cast; exact Int.natCast_natAbs j |>.symm
  rw [hr]
  exact_mod_cast hn
· intro hf N
  change (if |((0 : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ N then f 0 else 0) = 0
  rw [hf]
  split_ifs <;> rfl"

arguments.statement: ∀ f : KdVPlan.Coeff, (∀ (N : ℝ) (j : ℤ), ‖KdVPlan.cutoff N f j‖ ≤ ‖f j‖) ∧ (∀ (j : ℤ), ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, KdVPlan.cutoff (n : ℝ) f j = f j) ∧ (KdVPlan.ZeroMean f → ∀ N : ℝ, KdVPlan.ZeroMean (KdVPlan.cutoff N f))
arguments.proof:
intro f
refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
· intro N j
  unfold KdVPlan.cutoff
  split_ifs <;> simp
· intro j
  filter_upwards [Filter.eventually_ge_atTop j.natAbs] with n hn
  apply if_pos
  have hr : |(j : ℝ)| = (j.natAbs : ℝ) := by rw [← Int.cast_abs, ← Int.natCast_natAbs]; simp only [Int.cast_natCast]
  rw [hr]
  exact_mod_cast hn
· intro hf N
  change (if |((0 : ℤ) : ℝ)| ≤ N then f 0 else 0) = 0
  rw [hf]
  split_ifs <;> rfl

11: /-!
12: # Tannery's theorem
13: 
14: Tannery's theorem gives a sufficient criterion for the limit of an infinite sum (with respect to
15: an auxiliary parameter) to equal the sum of the pointwise limits. See
16: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tannery%27s_theorem. It is a special case of the dominated convergence
17: theorem (with the measure chosen to be the counting measure); but we give here a direct proof, in
18: order to avoid some unnecessary hypotheses that appear when specialising the general
19: measure-theoretic result.
20: -/
21: 
22: public section
23: 
24: open Filter Topology
25: 
26: set_option linter.style.whitespace false in -- manual alignment is not recognised
27: /-- **Tannery's theorem**: topological sums commute with termwise limits, when the norms of the
28: summands are eventually uniformly bounded by a summable function.
29: 
30: (This is the special case of the Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for the counting measure
31: on a discrete set. However, we prove it under somewhat weaker assumptions than the general
32: measure-theoretic result, e.g. `G` is not assumed to be an `ℝ`-vector space or second countable,
33: and the limit is along an arbitrary filter rather than `atTop ℕ`.)
34: 
35: See also:
36: * `MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence` (for general integrals, but
37:   with more assumptions on `G`)
38: * `continuous_tsum` (continuity of infinite sums in a parameter)
39: -/
40: lemma tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence {α β G : Type*} {𝓕 : Filter α}
41:     [NormedAddCommGroup G] [CompleteSpace G]
42:     {f : α → β → G} {g : β → G} {bound : β → ℝ} (h_sum : Summable bound)
43:     (hab : ∀ k : β, Tendsto (f · k) 𝓕 (𝓝 (g k)))
44:     (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in 𝓕, ∀ k, ‖f n k‖ ≤ bound k) :
45:     Tendsto (∑' k, f · k) 𝓕 (𝓝 (∑' k, g k)) := by
46:   -- WLOG β is nonempty
47:   rcases isEmpty_or_nonempty β
48:   · simpa only [tsum_empty] using tendsto_const_nhds
49:   -- WLOG 𝓕 ≠ ⊥
50:   rcases 𝓕.eq_or_neBot with rfl | _
51:   · simp only [tendsto_bot]
52:   -- Auxiliary lemmas
53:   have h_g_le (k : β) : ‖g k‖ ≤ bound k :=
54:     le_of_tendsto (tendsto_norm.comp (hab k)) <| h_bound.mono (fun n h => h k)
55:   have h_sumg : Summable (‖g ·‖) :=
56:     h_sum.of_norm_bounded (fun k ↦ (norm_norm (g k)).symm ▸ h_g_le k)
57:   have h_suma : ∀ᶠ n in 𝓕, Summable (‖f n ·‖) := by
58:     filter_upwards [h_bound] with n h
59:     exact h_sum.of_norm_bounded <| by simpa only [norm_norm] using h
60:   -- Now main proof, by an `ε / 3` argument
61:   rw [Metric.tendsto_nhds]
62:   intro ε hε
63:   let ⟨S, hS⟩ := h_sum
64:   obtain ⟨T, hT⟩ : ∃ (T : Finset β), dist (∑ b ∈ T, bound b) S < ε / 3 := by
65:     rw [HasSum, Metric.tendsto_nhds] at hS
66:     classical exact Eventually.exists <| hS _ (by positivity)
67:   have h1 : ∑' (k : (Tᶜ : Set β)), bound k < ε / 3 := by
68:     calc _ ≤ ‖∑' (k : (Tᶜ : Set β)), bound k‖ := Real.le_norm_self _
69:          _ = ‖S - ∑ b ∈ T, bound b‖           := congrArg _ ?_
70:          _ < ε / 3                            := by rwa [dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev] at hT
71:     simpa only [h_sum.sum_add_tsum_compl, eq_sub_iff_add_eq'] using hS.tsum_eq
72:   have h2 : Tendsto (∑ k ∈ T, f · k) 𝓕 (𝓝 (T.sum g)) := tendsto_finsetSum _ (fun i _ ↦ hab i)
73:   rw [Metric.tendsto_nhds] at h2
74:   filter_upwards [h2 (ε / 3) (by positivity), h_suma, h_bound] with n hn h_suma h_bound
75:   rw [dist_eq_norm, ← h_suma.of_norm.tsum_sub h_sumg.of_norm,
76:     ← (h_suma.of_norm.sub h_sumg.of_norm).sum_add_tsum_compl (s := T),
77:     (by ring : ε = ε / 3 + (ε / 3 + ε / 3))]
78:   refine (norm_add_le _ _).trans_lt (add_lt_add ?_ ?_)
79:   · simpa only [dist_eq_norm, Finset.sum_sub_distrib] using hn
80:   · rw [(h_suma.subtype _).of_norm.tsum_sub (h_sumg.subtype _).of_norm]
81:     refine (norm_sub_le _ _).trans_lt (add_lt_add ?_ ?_)
82:     · refine ((norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm (h_suma.subtype _)).trans ?_).trans_lt h1
83:       exact (h_suma.subtype _).tsum_le_tsum (h_bound ·) (h_sum.subtype _)
84:     · refine ((norm_tsum_le_tsum_norm <| h_sumg.subtype _).trans ?_).trans_lt h1
85:       exact (h_sumg.subtype _).tsum_le_tsum (h_g_le ·) (h_sum.subtype _)"}

169: /-- Lebesgue dominated convergence theorem for filters with a countable basis -/
170: nonrec theorem tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence {ι} {l : Filter ι}
171:     [l.IsCountablyGenerated] {F : ι → ℝ → E} (bound : ℝ → ℝ)
172:     (hF_meas : ∀ᶠ n in l, AEStronglyMeasurable (F n) (μ.restrict (Ι a b)))
173:     (h_bound : ∀ᶠ n in l, ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ι a b → ‖F n x‖ ≤ bound x)
174:     (bound_integrable : IntervalIntegrable bound μ a b)
175:     (h_lim : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ι a b → Tendsto (fun n => F n x) l (𝓝 (f x))) :
176:     Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x in a..b, F n x ∂μ) l (𝓝 <| ∫ x in a..b, f x ∂μ) := by
177:   simp only [intervalIntegrable_iff, intervalIntegral_eq_integral_uIoc,
178:     ← ae_restrict_iff' (α := ℝ) (μ := μ) measurableSet_uIoc] at *
179:   exact tendsto_const_nhds.smul <|

72: def IntervalIntegrable (f : ℝ → ε) (μ : Measure ℝ) (a b : ℝ) : Prop :=
73:   IntegrableOn f (Ioc a b) μ ∧ IntegrableOn f (Ioc b a) μ

75: /-!
76: ## Basic iff's for `IntervalIntegrable`
77: -/
78: section
79: 
80: variable [PseudoMetrizableSpace ε] {f : ℝ → ε} {a b : ℝ} {μ : Measure ℝ}
81: 
82: /-- A function is interval integrable with respect to a given measure `μ` on `a..b` if and
83:   only if it is integrable on `uIoc a b` with respect to `μ`. This is an equivalent
84:   definition of `IntervalIntegrable`. -/
85: theorem intervalIntegrable_iff : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b ↔ IntegrableOn f (Ι a b) μ := by
86:   rw [uIoc_eq_union, integrableOn_union, IntervalIntegrable]
87: 
88: /-- If a function is interval integrable with respect to a given measure `μ` on `a..b` then
89:   it is integrable on `uIoc a b` with respect to `μ`. -/
90: theorem IntervalIntegrable.def' (h : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) : IntegrableOn f (Ι a b) μ :=
91:   intervalIntegrable_iff.mp h
92: 
93: theorem intervalIntegrable_congr_ae {g : ℝ → ε} (h : f =ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ι a b)] g) :
94:     IntervalIntegrable f μ a b ↔ IntervalIntegrable g μ a b := by
95:   rw [intervalIntegrable_iff, integrableOn_congr_fun_ae h, intervalIntegrable_iff]
96: 
97: theorem intervalIntegrable_congr_uIoo [NullSingletonClass μ] {g : ℝ → ε} (h : EqOn f g (uIoo a b)) :
98:     IntervalIntegrable f μ a b ↔ IntervalIntegrable g μ a b := by
99:   apply intervalIntegrable_congr_ae
100:   rw [uIoc, ← restrict_Ioo_eq_restrict_Ioc]
101:   apply ae_restrict_of_forall_mem measurableSet_Ioo h
102: 
103: theorem IntervalIntegrable.congr_ae {g : ℝ → ε} (hf : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b)
104:     (h : f =ᵐ[μ.restrict (Ι a b)] g) :
105:     IntervalIntegrable g μ a b := by
106:   rwa [← intervalIntegrable_congr_ae h]
107: 
108: theorem IntervalIntegrable.congr_uIoo [NullSingletonClass μ] {g : ℝ → ε}
109:     (hf : IntervalIntegrable f μ a b) (h : EqOn f g (uIoo a b)) : IntervalIntegrable g μ a b :=
110:   intervalIntegrable_congr_uIoo h |>.mp hf
111: 
112: theorem intervalIntegrable_congr {g : ℝ → ε} (h : EqOn f g (Ι a b)) :
113:     IntervalIntegrable f μ a b ↔ IntervalIntegrable g μ a b :=
114:   intervalIntegrable_congr_ae <| (ae_restrict_mem measurableSet_uIoc).mono h
